monitors.name: coldread-floor
monitors.reads: WORKING TREE: python3 .ufo/evidence/round-21/coldread/measure.py (which imports .ufo/evidence/round-18/measure.py from the tree); only the ledger/data are REV-bound
monitors.subject: the cold-read calibration score and credited section count at REV
monitors.catches: credit loss at REV (RED at base: score=6 credited=46)
monitors.defect: FINDING A1: no self-pin anywhere in the chain (round-18 measure.py has no self_pin, the round-21 wrapper has none, and the JSON payload carries no pass/self_pin field), so an uncommitted edit to the working-tree wrapper turns this line green at a REV that does not earn it (demo 2: score=8 credited=64 ok at c3e2ca9f, whose clean bytes read 6/46). This is the C1-axis monitor and the only RED at base.
monitors.fix_line: 15: precede it with `git diff --quiet "$REV" -- .ufo/evidence/round-18/measure.py .ufo/evidence/round-21/coldread/measure.py || s=RED`, or add a self_pin arm to the round-21 wrapper and require self_pin=1 in the parse

monitors.name: r45-freshness

monitors.subject: fresh (verified+agreed, undisputed) census rows over the population
monitors.catches: a stale SOURCES row or a disputed review; zero headroom (fresh=71 == floor 71)
monitors.defect: FINDING A2: the counter prints self_pin=0 and C1_R45_PASS=false after a working-tree edit, and the monitor still prints ok because its grep extracts only population=/fresh= (demo 1). The self-pin guard exists and is thrown away.
monitors.fix_line: 17: add `self_pin=[0-9]+` and `C1_R45_PASS=[a-z]+` to the grep, and require self_pin=1 and C1_R45_PASS=true in the test at line 18 instead of recomputing the ratio

monitors.name: r45-coverage

monitors.subject: round-45 rows S256,S257 and their two knowledge entries, indexed
monitors.catches: removal of a round-45 knowledge entry or its README index line; also any tree drift of the counter (demo 6: self_pin=0 -> RED)
monitors.defect: none for contamination; brittle only in that the exact string rows=2 entries=2 turns RED if C0 adds a knowledge entry whose line-1 source: cites S256 or S257
monitors.fix_line: 20: none required; if the count arm is to survive legitimate growth, compare against the BASE counts rather than the literals 2/2

monitors.name: S160-count

monitors.catches: deletion or duplication of the S160 row
monitors.defect: a one-row canary out of 140: any of the other 139 rows can be deleted or rewritten (same id, different content) and this line stays green; the id-set arm it pretends to be is sources-not-shrunk's job
monitors.fix_line: 21-22: replace with a set check that every BASE row id is still present at REV (git show BASE:corpus/SOURCES.md ids subset of REV ids), not a single literal

monitors.name: registry-rows-not-below-140

monitors.defect: the constant 140 is the base count hard-coded, duplicating sources-not-shrunk (line 47-49) which derives it from BASE; two monitors on one surface with different semantics, and a legitimate retirement of a row below 140 reads as harm while a rewrite of every row reads as clean
monitors.fix_line: 24: derive from BASE (`R0=$(git show "$BASE:corpus/SOURCES.md" | grep -cE ...)`) or delete the monitor as redundant with sources-not-shrunk

monitors.name: tools-scope
monitors.reads: REV bytes (git diff --name-status BASE REV -- tools)
monitors.subject: the set of tools/ paths changed between BASE and REV against an allowlist
monitors.catches: an edit to a tools/ file outside the allowlist
monitors.defect: FINDING A3: name-status only. An entry added since BASE is reported A: whatever its content, so the round's new gate can be replaced by a no-op and the allowlist still admits it (demo 5b: A:tools/receipt-revision-gate.py ok, bytes `sys.exit(0)`). An empty set is also ok, so a REV that adds no tool at all passes.
monitors.fix_line: 30: for A: entries, compare the blob to the freeze commit's blob (`[ "$(git rev-parse "$REV:$p")" = "$(git rev-parse "c3e2ca9f:$p")" ]`); treat the empty set as RED when the round's contract declares an added tool

monitors.name: registry-rows-not-shrunk

monitors.subject: registry row count monotonicity (base=56)
monitors.defect: count-only: a row rewritten in place (same id, different command/path) is invisible
monitors.fix_line: 34: add an id-set arm (BASE ids subset of REV ids) beside the count

monitors.name: r49-generator-capability
monitors.reads: REV bytes (git show REV:tools/pbt-staged-id.py and staged-id-guard.py into $SCR, run from $SCR)
monitors.subject: 400-case property run at seed 4949, exact expected line including the class histogram
monitors.catches: any change to the generator or guard that moves the class distribution or the violation count
monitors.defect: exact full-line equality: a legitimate improvement to the generator is indistinguishable from a regression, and the line cannot say which arm moved
monitors.fix_line: 37: compare `cases=400 violations=0 counterexample=none` and the histogram as two separate arms so a failure names itself

monitors.name: r50-shrinker-selftest
monitors.reads: REV bytes (git show REV:tools/shrink-case.py into $SCR, run from $SCR)
monitors.subject: the shrinker's own selftest exit line
monitors.catches: a crash (empty output -> RED, demo 4) and any reported failure
monitors.defect: FINDING B1: the guard is the suffix glob `*" failed=0"`, so a shrinker whose selftest runs zero cases passes (demo 4: `cases=0 failed=0` -> ok). The monitor is vacuous on the input class it claims to guard.
monitors.fix_line: 41: `case "$K" in *"cases=14 failed=0")` (or parse cases and require cases >= 14)

monitors.name: r53-scratch-hygiene
monitors.reads: REV bytes (git grep -c at REV over tools/)
monitors.subject: occurrences of `dir = "/tmp"` in tools/
monitors.catches: one syntactic form of hard-coded /tmp use
monitors.defect: FINDING B2: fails OPEN. `git grep` exits 128 on an unparsable REV and the awk still sums to 0, so an unmeasurable run prints tmp_hits=0 ok (demo 3). The pattern also misses `/tmp` outside an assignment to a variable named dir.
monitors.fix_line: 42: capture the exit status and RED on >1 (`git grep ...; rc=$?; [ $rc -le 1 ] || s=RED`), and widen the pattern to `/tmp` anywhere in tools/
